clue.text: Last call at Westminster when the Tardis returns to base

parts.note: the Tardis is the time machine of Doctor Who, so it stands for its owner
to return to base

explanation.surface: A doorkeeper's closing cry in Parliament coincides with a TV time machine heading back to its base.
explanation.walkthrough: The doorkeepers of the House of Commons traditionally call this at the end of a sitting; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional cry of the Commons doorkeepers when the House rises, so it is the last call at Westminster.

clue.text: The rain is now falling moderately

indicators.note: rain falling comes down in a jumble, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather report: the rain has started coming down, but not heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' looks like part of the weather picture; it tells you to rearrange THE RAIN IS NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something only as far as is sensible is doing it in moderation, an adverbial idiom.

clue.text: Yet more contempt generated by such presumption?

definitions.text: Yet more contempt generated by such presumption?

parts.words: Yet more contempt generated by such presumption?
parts.note: plays on the proverb that familiarity breeds contempt: an excess of it, taking liberties, would breed even more

explanation.definitionFit: Excessive informality, taking liberties with someone, is presumption, and by the proverb it breeds contempt.

clue.text: Abhorrence about one stage in fungal development

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes round it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: odium is hatred or abhorrence
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Disgust at a particular phase in the growth of a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: In mycology this term names a thin-walled spore form, a phase in the life of certain fungi such as mildews.

clue.text: The governor's a tyrant when lifting the gin

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word raises it, so its letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A ruler is shown to be despotic when he raises his glass of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' reads as the drink; it is the old word for a snare. The definition describes the word's two senses together: a provincial governor of ancient Persia, and by extension a petty despot.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a provincial governor in ancient Persia, the word now also means any subordinate ruler acting despotically.

clue.text: Beam of light ran somewhere within

indicators.note: says the answer lies inside the run of words that precedes it

explanation.surface: Daylight ran through some part of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam of light' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Beam', and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal crossbar above a door or window is a structural beam.

clue.text: One of the Shakers making or breaking the circuit?

definitions.meaning: someone who shakes or quivers; the Shakers sect were known for trembling in worship
a vibrating electrical contact, as in a bell or induction coil, that repeatedly makes and breaks the circuit

explanation.surface: A member of a religious sect switching an electrical circuit on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who quakes is literally one who shakes, and the electrical name is for a vibrating contact switch.

clue.text: Oil state ruler thus consecrated?

parts.note: a monarch is consecrated by being smeared with holy oil, so a sheikh of an oil state might jokingly be thought consecrated with oil

explanation.definitionFit: Being consecrated by ritual application of oil, as at a coronation, is exactly this word's sense.

clue.text: Hysteric, overstretched soprano heard as La Bohème?

parts.note: a soprano pushed beyond her range would be screaming

indicators.note: says the letters are what a word sounds like, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Mimi is the soprano heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème

explanation.surface: A singer pushed too far sounds hysterical as the heroine of Puccini's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimì, the heroine of La Bohème, gives the sound of the second word, spelt MEEMIE.
explanation.definitionFit: This colloquial phrase means a hysterical person, or a fit of hysterics.

clue.text: Moriarty his chosen subject?

definitions.meaning: Professor Moriarty, Sherlock Holmes's enemy, is the criminal genius behind every plot
the BBC quiz show in which each contestant answers questions on a chosen specialist subject

explanation.surface: Asks whether Professor Moriarty is the topic a quiz contestant has picked.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal genius who plans everything is the word for Moriarty; the quiz show carries the same name.

clue.text: Act in walk-on parts?

definitions.meaning: to perform on stage as an actor
literally, to step on the planks of a stage, parts of it you walk on

explanation.surface: Taking minor roles as an extra on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a stage actor is idiomatically to step on the planks of the stage.

clue.text: See above
Done Maugham's bone of contention? Sadly, some abandoned his book

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are disturbed and rearranged
the letters of the word some are dropped from the mixed pool

parts.note: taken as written, the letter pool to be rearranged
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A grumble that the novelist Maugham has been done out of his point of dispute, with some of his work given up.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange DONE MAUGHAMS BONE OF ('Sadly'), take away the letters of SOME ('abandoned'), and the remaining fourteen letters spell the title; 'contention' is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1915 novel is Somerset Maugham's best-known work, so it is his book.

clue.text: Church or Tallis composition giving support for the singer

indicators.note: a composition puts things together in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church performs a piece by the composer Tallis, which upholds the vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like a musical work by Tallis, but it signals rearranging OR TALLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat in the chancel for a chorister is a support in the literal sense for a singer.

clue.text: See 1
Kentish Man, I'm holding uranium element

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE
Len is a man's name

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A man from Kent announces he has some uranium, a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a non-metallic chemical element, number 34.

clue.text: See 1
Close affiliations with pyjamas have they?

definitions.text: Close affiliations with pyjamas have they?

parts.note: nigh means near or close
ties are connections or affiliations

explanation.surface: Asks which garments are closely related to pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: night garments are close relations of pyjamas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightdresses are bedtime wear, closely related to pyjamas.

clue.text: State declaration of my intent; one is no pushover

indicators.note: the word no is pushed over in front of the word is, swapping their order

parts.note: I'll is short for 'I will', a statement of intention
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares their intention and insists they are not easily beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushover' reads as an easy victim, the surface's boast; here it is an instruction to swap the order of the last two little words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a state of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: A good measure of habitation in Aquitaine

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A fair amount of housing in south-west France.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in the Aquitaine region of south-west France, a place of habitation.

clue.text: Cheat taking a cut

definitions.meaning: slang for cheating or swindling them
a carving tool that cuts into wood or stone

explanation.surface: A swindler helps himself to a share of the money.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb means to swindle, and the tool is a cutting blade.

clue.text: For hard work one's a byword, for art? No judge unfortunately

definitions.text: For hard work one's a byword

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately are upset, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard worker is renowned, but there's no judge for artistic merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for art?' is linked by 'for'; mix ART, NO and J (judge) as 'unfortunately' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'work like a Trojan' makes this people the byword for hard labour.

clue.text: "13 24 and don't ___"

parts.note: the numbers point to other entries, completing the old catchphrase to a coachman, urging speed

explanation.walkthrough: 13 is HOME and 24 is JAMES, giving the jocular command "Home, James, and don't ...", an order to drive fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase ends with telling the driver not to hold back his team, that is, to go full speed.

clue.text: Exploited employee of the Washington Post?

parts.note: the Washington Post is American, US
a newspaper employee is an editor, ED

explanation.surface: A journalist at an American newspaper was taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploited and taken advantage of are synonyms of this past participle.

clue.text: Where to hole a vessel among the fleet

parts.note: amid means among
a fleet is a number of ships

explanation.surface: Instructions for torpedoing a boat in the middle of a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Midway along a ship is the most effective place for a torpedo strike.

clue.text: Writer's block, he's unable to begin

parts.note: to jam is to block

indicators.note: the first letter is lost, so the word cannot begin

parts.note: taken as he and s, the letters HES

explanation.surface: A writer is stuck: he can't get started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' looks like one phrase; 'Writer' is the definition (Henry James) and 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was the American-born novelist, a celebrated writer.

clue.text: Billy Connolly's one in convict's clutches

indicators.note: one piece placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: a lag is a convict, with s added
the Scottish comedian Billy Connolly would say yin for one

explanation.surface: A single person caught in a convict's grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' reads as a grip; it is the definition, sets of eggs laid.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a set of eggs laid together, so batches of eggs are these.

clue.text: Left one with desire to embrace Society for Preservation of Bats, when pressed

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: one word embracing another wraps around it

parts.note: need is desire or want

explanation.surface: A society for protecting bats seems to be in a hurry for someone to join.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressing these seeds gives the oil rubbed into cricket bats to preserve them; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax seeds, when crushed, give the oil used to treat and protect cricket bats.
